title: A water droplet on two papers
source: School paper question (water droplet dropped onto papers A and B)
pageIntro: Drop one droplet on each paper and wait. Then read the droplet and the wet patch on each paper.
stem:
A similar size water droplet is dropped onto papers A and B. The observation is as shown below after five minutes.

Which one of the following statements is correct?
figure: <svg viewBox='0 0 520 200' role='img' aria-label='Paper A has a water droplet with a small wet patch around it. Paper B has a wet patch and no water droplet.'><g><text class='lbl' x='130' y='26' text-anchor='middle'>A</text><path class='sl' d='M34 50 L206 42 L226 142 L52 152 z'/><text class='lbl sm' x='64' y='70'>paper</text><ellipse class='ln fa' stroke-dasharray='5 4' cx='130' cy='96' rx='22' ry='16'/><ellipse class='ln fa hot' cx='130' cy='96' rx='9' ry='7'/><text class='lbl sm' x='130' y='172' text-anchor='middle'>water droplet</text><text class='lbl sm' x='130' y='188' text-anchor='middle'>wet patch</text></g><g><text class='lbl' x='390' y='26' text-anchor='middle'>B</text><path class='sl' d='M294 50 L466 42 L486 142 L312 152 z'/><text class='lbl sm' x='324' y='70'>paper</text><ellipse class='ln fa' stroke-dasharray='5 4' cx='390' cy='96' rx='42' ry='30'/><text class='lbl sm' x='390' y='172' text-anchor='middle'>wet patch with</text><text class='lbl sm' x='390' y='188' text-anchor='middle'>no water droplet</text></g></svg>
hints: Look at each paper after five minutes. Which paper still has water sitting on top, and which paper has water that went in?
A wet patch is the evidence that water has gone into the paper. Which paper has the bigger wet patch?
key: Water sitting on top of a paper has not been absorbed. A wet patch shows that water went in. Waterproof means no water goes in at all, so a paper with any wet patch is not waterproof.

options.text: Paper A is more absorbent than paper B.
options.pick: Paper A still has a droplet with water in it, so it looks like the paper that is holding the water.
options.why: The droplet on A is water sitting on top, not water that has been absorbed. B has no droplet left and the largest wet patch, so all of its water went into the paper. B is the more absorbent paper.
clash: Your readings: A kept most of its droplet and had a small wet patch. B's droplet was gone and its wet patch was large.

options.text: Paper A is waterproof but paper B is not.
options.pick: The droplet on A is still there after five minutes, so A looks as if it kept the water out, while B soaked it up.
options.why: Waterproof means a material does not absorb water. A has a wet patch and its droplet got smaller, so some water went into it. A absorbed less than B, but it is not waterproof. Only the plastic sheet, with no wet patch at all, absorbed nothing.
clash: Your readings: A's droplet got smaller and left a small wet patch, so A absorbed some water.

options.text: Paper B is more absorbent than paper A.
options.pick: Compare the water on top with the water that went in: B's droplet is gone and its wet patch is the biggest, while most of A's droplet is still on top.
options.why: Absorbent means it takes in water. B took in all of its droplet and shows the larger wet patch. A took in only a little and shows a small wet patch. So B is more absorbent than A.

options.text: Paper B is less waterproof than paper A.
options.pick: It sounds like (3) said another way: B soaks up the water, so it seems less waterproof than A.
options.why: Waterproof is not a matter of more or less: it means the material does not absorb water at all. Both papers have a wet patch, so water went into both and neither is waterproof. What the observation shows is how much each absorbed, and B absorbed more.
clash: Your readings: both A and B have a wet patch, so neither paper is waterproof.
